title: Tomates Farcies
subtitle: Baked tomatoes stuffed with herbed minced pork and beef
excerpt: Large tomatoes hollowed and filled with a garlicky pork and beef mixture, then baked until the tops colour and the filling is cooked through. A French summer staple.
sourceNotes: Classic French home cooking; found across all regions. Often served with steamed rice.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Fill the tomatoes up to 4 hours ahead. Keep chilled and bake when ready.

content.text: Tomates farcies are a simple French baked dish of large tomatoes filled with herbed minced meat. Use the ripest tomatoes you can find so the shells hold their shape in the oven. Do not pack the filling too tightly or the tomatoes will burst.
Heat the oven to 190C. Slice the tops off the tomatoes and set the lids aside. Scoop out the seeds and pulp with a spoon. Chop the pulp roughly and set it aside.
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Tip into a bowl and leave to cool.
Add both minces, the parsley, thyme, breadcrumbs, beaten egg and half the reserved tomato pulp to the bowl. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Sit the tomato shells in a roasting tin. Fill each one generously with the meat mixture. Do not press down hard. Replace the lids at an angle.
Pour the remaining tomato pulp into the base of the tin. Drizzle the tops with a little olive oil.
Bake for 45 minutes until the filling is cooked through and the tops are lightly coloured. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

items.symptom: The tomato shells collapse during baking.
items.cause: The tomatoes were over-ripe or the filling was packed in too firmly.
items.fix: Choose firm, ripe tomatoes and fill loosely so the flesh can hold the filling's weight.

items.cause: Too little tomato pulp was added to the mixture.
items.fix: Add 2 tablespoons of the scooped pulp back into the filling before stuffing next time.

items.symptom: The top browns but the filling is still pink inside.
items.cause: The tomatoes were very large and the oven runs hot.
items.fix: Cover the tin loosely with foil and return to the oven for a further 10 to 15 minutes.
